```{python}
tier_change_major = tier_change.filter(pl.col("tier_a") != "under $1,200").height

show(years_differ, caption="Fiscal years where crediting shared legacy gifts changes major donor counts")
```

The two versions differ in only `{python} n(years_differ.height)` fiscal years, all before FY2021, and by at most `{python} n(max_diff)` major donors in any year. `{python} n(tier_change.height)` person-years change tier, almost all because a small legacy gift disappears under option D, and only `{python} n(tier_change_major)` of them are major donor-years. The choice between A and D has no practical effect, so the rest of the notebook uses option A. Option D will be rerun once more when conversion rates are calculated.

### Summary for Modeling

- Individual giving totals reconcile exactly with Unite revenue, and legacy history links cleanly to Unite donors, so the panel is a sound base for both the target and giving features.
- Major giving is much rarer than the problem statement assumed: about `{python} n(recent["major_donors"].mean())` major donors a year out of roughly `{python} n(round(recent["donors"].mean(), -3))` donors. The conversion base rate in the next section will be correspondingly low.
- Almost no donors give just below $1,200, and major donors mostly give exact tier amounts with a soft credit involved. Becoming a major donor is a jump in dollars, and soft credits need careful timing so they do not leak the outcome.
- The upper tiers are too thin to model separately.
- Spouse-shared legacy gifts do not affect the results.

## Major Donors and Conversion

### Definitions

The model will be run at a prediction date and asked which current non-major donors will become major donors. I set the prediction date at the end of a fiscal year, so a cohort is named by the fiscal year that just ended (FY t).

- **Eligible donors:** constituents who gave in FY t and gave less than $1,200 that year.
- **Outcomes:** the donor gives $1,200 or more in FY t+1 (the 12 month outcome), in any year from FY t+1 to FY t+3 (within 3 years), or in any year from FY t+1 to FY t+5 (within 5 years).
- **Groups:** eligible donors who were major donors in any year before FY t are "former majors." Everyone else is "never major." Results are reported for both, since lapsed major donors coming back are a different kind of prospect than first-time major donors.

A cohort can only be scored if all of its outcome years are in the data, so the last usable cohort is FY2025 for 12 months, FY2023 for 3 years, and FY2021 for 5 years. Cohorts start in FY1999, when the legacy records become complete.

```{python}
#| label: cohorts

LAST_FY = int(panel["fy"].max())
WINDOWS = {1: "12 months", 3: "within 3 years", 5: "within 5 years"}

def cohort(panel_df, t, window):
    # eligible donors at the end of FY t, with their prior-year total and outcome
    majors = panel_df.filter(pl.col("major")).select("constituent_id", "fy")
    former = majors.filter(pl.col("fy") < t)["constituent_id"].unique().implode()
    converted = majors.filter(pl.col("fy").is_between(t + 1, t + window))["constituent_id"].unique().implode()
    return (
        panel_df.filter((pl.col("fy") == t) & ~pl.col("major"))
        .select("constituent_id", prior_total=pl.col("total"))
        .with_columns(
            former_major=pl.col("constituent_id").is_in(former),
            converted=pl.col("constituent_id").is_in(converted),
            t=pl.lit(t),
            window=pl.lit(window),
        )
    )

def build_cohorts(panel_df):
    return pl.concat([
        cohort(panel_df, t, w) for w in WINDOWS for t in range(1999, LAST_FY - w + 1)
    ])

cohorts = build_cohorts(panel)
cohorts = cohorts.with_columns(
    era=pl.when(pl.col("t") >= 2021).then(pl.lit("FY2021 on")).otherwise(pl.lit("FY1999 to FY2020")),
    group=pl.when(pl.col("former_major")).then(pl.lit("former major")).otherwise(pl.lit("never major")),
)
```

### Conversion Base Rates

```{python}
#| label: base-rates
#| fig-height: 3.5
# conversion rate for each cohort and outcome window

rates_by_cohort = (
    cohorts.group_by("window", "t")
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"),
                  outcome=pl.col("window").replace_strict(WINDOWS))
    .sort("window", "t")
)

(
    ggplot(rates_by_cohort.to_pandas(), aes("t", "rate", color="outcome"))
    + geom_line()
    + geom_point(size=1.2)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=2020.5, linetype="dotted", color="grey")
    + scale_y_continuous(labels=lambda b: [f"{v:.2%}" for v in b])
    + labs(x="Cohort (fiscal year that just ended)", y="Share of eligible donors who convert",
           color="Outcome", title="Conversion to major giving by cohort")
)
```

```{python}
#| label: pooled-rates
# conversion pooled across cohorts, by era and by never-major versus former-major donors

def pooled(df, by):
    return (
        df.group_by(by)
        .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
        .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
    )

pooled_rates = (
    pl.concat([
        pooled(cohorts, ["window", "era"]).with_columns(group=pl.lit("all eligible")),
        pooled(cohorts, ["window", "era", "group"]),
    ], how="diagonal")
    .with_columns(outcome=pl.col("window").replace_strict(WINDOWS))
    .sort("window", "era", "group")
    .select("outcome", "era", "group", "eligible", "converters", "rate")
)

def rate_of(window, era, group):
    row = pooled_rates.filter((pl.col("outcome") == WINDOWS[window]) & (pl.col("era") == era) & (pl.col("group") == group))
    return row.row(0, named=True)

r12 = rate_of(1, "FY2021 on", "all eligible")
r12_never = rate_of(1, "FY2021 on", "never major")
r12_former = rate_of(1, "FY2021 on", "former major")
r3 = rate_of(3, "FY2021 on", "all eligible")
r5 = rate_of(5, "FY2021 on", "all eligible")
r12_legacy = rate_of(1, "FY1999 to FY2020", "all eligible")
rates_12_all = rates_by_cohort.filter(pl.col("window") == 1)
recent_12 = rates_12_all.filter(pl.col("t") >= 2021)

show(pooled_rates, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Conversion rates by outcome window and donor group")
```

Conversion is rare. For cohorts from FY2021 on, `{python} pct(r12["rate"], 2)` of eligible donors become major donors the next year (`{python} n(r12["converters"])` converters out of `{python} n(r12["eligible"])` eligible donor-years), or about `{python} n(recent_12["converters"].mean())` people per year out of roughly `{python} n(round(recent_12["eligible"].mean(), -3))`. The rate rises to `{python} pct(r3["rate"], 2)` within 3 years and `{python} pct(r5["rate"], 2)` within 5 years. The pooled legacy-era 12 month rate (`{python} pct(r12_legacy["rate"], 2)`) is similar, but single cohorts vary a lot. The 12 month rate ranges from `{python} pct(rates_12_all["rate"].min(), 2)` (FY`{python} rates_12_all.sort("rate")["t"][0]` cohort) to `{python} pct(rates_12_all["rate"].max(), 2)` (FY`{python} rates_12_all.sort("rate")["t"][-1]` cohort), and it was generally lower in the early 2000s than it is now. Among recent cohorts, FY2025 stands out, since its conversions happen in FY2026, the year after federal funding ended. With only around `{python} n(recent_12["converters"].mean())` converters a year, any one cohort's results will be noisy, which matters when models are compared on just a few backtest years.

### Former Major Donors

The split by group is the most important result in this section. Former majors convert at `{python} pct(r12_former["rate"])` over 12 months, compared with `{python} pct(r12_never["rate"], 3)` for donors who were never major. Former majors are only `{python} pct(r12_former["eligible"] / r12["eligible"])` of eligible donors, but they account for `{python} pct(r12_former["converters"] / r12["converters"])` of 12 month converters (`{python} n(r12_former["converters"])` of `{python} n(r12["converters"])`).

This matters for how the model is judged. Staff probably already know their lapsed major donors, so a list that mostly surfaces them would score well on recall without telling staff much they did not already know. The model's results should be reported for never-major donors on their own, and former major status should be an explicit feature so its effect is visible.

### Where New Major Donors Come From

The eligible population only includes people who gave in FY t. If many new major donors come from people who did not give that year, those people are outside the list no matter how good the model is. The table below sorts each year's new major donors (major this year but not last year) by where they came from.

```{python}
#| label: major-sources
# where each year's new major donors came from: gave last year, lapsed donor, or first gift

def major_sources(fy):
    majors_now = panel.filter((pl.col("fy") == fy) & pl.col("major"))["constituent_id"]
    majors_before = panel.filter((pl.col("fy") == fy - 1) & pl.col("major"))["constituent_id"]
    gave_last_year = panel.filter(pl.col("fy") == fy - 1)["constituent_id"]
    gave_ever_before = panel.filter(pl.col("fy") < fy)["constituent_id"].unique()
    new = majors_now.filter(~majors_now.is_in(majors_before.implode()))
    return {
        "fy": fy,
        "repeat_majors": majors_now.is_in(majors_before.implode()).sum(),
        "new_majors": new.len(),
        "gave_last_year": new.is_in(gave_last_year.implode()).sum(),
        "lapsed_donor": (~new.is_in(gave_last_year.implode()) & new.is_in(gave_ever_before.implode())).sum(),
        "first_gift": (~new.is_in(gave_ever_before.implode())).sum(),
    }

sources = pl.DataFrame([major_sources(fy) for fy in range(2017, LAST_FY + 1)])
src_recent = sources.filter(pl.col("fy") >= 2022).select(pl.exclude("fy").sum()).row(0, named=True)

show(sources, caption="Where each year's new major donors came from")
```

From FY2022 to FY2026 there were `{python} n(src_recent["new_majors"])` new major donors. `{python} n(src_recent["gave_last_year"])` of them (`{python} pct(src_recent["gave_last_year"] / src_recent["new_majors"])`) gave in the year before, so they were in the eligible population. Another `{python} n(src_recent["lapsed_donor"])` were lapsed donors who skipped the prior year, and only `{python} n(src_recent["first_gift"])` became major donors with their first gift. The eligibility rule therefore covers about nine in ten new major donors. The other tenth cannot appear on any list built from the eligible population, which is a small but real limit on how many of each year's new major donors the model can reach. Each year there are also `{python} n(sources.filter(pl.col("fy") >= 2022)["repeat_majors"].mean())` repeat major donors on average, who are outside this project's population because they are already major.

### Tier Reached at Conversion

```{python}
#| label: conversion-tiers
# tier reached in the conversion year by 12 month converters, FY2021 on

conv_tiers = (
    cohorts.filter((pl.col("window") == 1) & (pl.col("t") >= 2021) & pl.col("converted"))
    .select("constituent_id", fy=pl.col("t") + 1)
    .join(panel.select("constituent_id", "fy", "tier"), on=["constituent_id", "fy"])
    .group_by("tier").agg(converters=pl.len())
    .with_columns(share=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("converters").sum())
    .sort("tier")
)
tier_conv = {str(r["tier"]): r["converters"] for r in conv_tiers.iter_rows(named=True)}
conv_top = sum(v for k, v in tier_conv.items() if k in ("$5,000", "$10,000", "$15,000+"))

show(conv_tiers, pct_cols=["share"], caption="Tier reached by 12 month converters")
```

Of the `{python} n(r12["converters"])` 12 month converters since FY2021, `{python} n(tier_conv.get("$1,200", 0))` reach the $1,200 tier, `{python} n(tier_conv.get("$2,000", 0))` reach $2,000, and only `{python} n(conv_top)` reach $5,000 or more. This supports collapsing the top three tiers, and it means the tier part of the model is mostly a choice between $1,200 and $2,000.

### Prior-Year Giving and the 25% Target

The problem statement sets a target of at least 25% of converters in the top 10% of the ranked list, to be confirmed once the base rate is known. A useful first check is how a very simple ranking does: sort eligible donors by how much they gave in FY t. If that alone beats 25%, the target is too easy to show that a model adds value.

```{python}
#| label: prior-giving-bands
# 12 month conversion by band of prior-year giving, FY2021 to FY2025 cohorts

BAND_LABELS = ["$60 or less", "$61 to $120", "$121 to $240", "$241 to $500", "$501 to $750", "over $750"]
bands_12 = (
    cohorts.filter((pl.col("window") == 1) & (pl.col("t") >= 2021))
    .with_columns(prior_band=pl.col("prior_total").cut([60, 120, 240, 500, 750], labels=BAND_LABELS)
                  .cast(pl.Enum(BAND_LABELS)))
    .group_by("prior_band")
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"),
                  share_of_converters=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("converters").sum())
    .sort("prior_band")
)
top_band = bands_12.filter(pl.col("prior_band") == "$501 to $750").row(0, named=True)

show(bands_12, pct_cols=["rate", "share_of_converters"], pct_digits=2, caption="12 month conversion by band of prior-year giving")
```

```{python}
#| label: simple-ranking

def ranked_recall(df, k):
    # expected recall when ranking by prior_total, with random order inside ties at the cutoff
    df = df.sort("prior_total", descending=True)
    cut = df["prior_total"][k - 1]
    above = df.filter(pl.col("prior_total") > cut)
    tied = df.filter(pl.col("prior_total") == cut)
    expected = above["converted"].sum() + tied["converted"].sum() * (k - above.height) / tied.height
    return expected / df["converted"].sum()

recall_rows = []
for (w, t), d in cohorts.filter(pl.col("t") >= 2021).group_by("window", "t"):
    never = d.filter(~pl.col("former_major"))
    recall_rows.append({
        "outcome": WINDOWS[w], "cohort": t, "eligible": d.height, "converters": d["converted"].sum(),
        "recall_top_10pct": ranked_recall(d, round(d.height * 0.10)),
        "recall_top_1000": ranked_recall(d, 1000),
        "never_major_recall_top_10pct": ranked_recall(never, round(never.height * 0.10)),
    })
simple_recall = pl.DataFrame(recall_rows).sort("outcome", "cohort")
rec12 = simple_recall.filter(pl.col("outcome") == "12 months")
rec3 = simple_recall.filter(pl.col("outcome") == "within 3 years")
rec5 = simple_recall.filter(pl.col("outcome") == "within 5 years")

show(simple_recall, pct_cols=["recall_top_10pct", "recall_top_1000", "never_major_recall_top_10pct"], caption="Recall of a ranking by prior-year giving, by outcome and cohort")
```

Prior-year giving is a strong signal even though nobody gives just under $1,200. Donors who gave $501 to $750 convert at `{python} pct(top_band["rate"])` and make up `{python} pct(top_band["share_of_converters"])` of 12 month converters, while donors under $240 almost never convert. As a result, the one-variable ranking puts `{python} pct(rec12["recall_top_10pct"].min())` to `{python} pct(rec12["recall_top_10pct"].max())` of 12 month converters in the top 10%, `{python} pct(rec3["recall_top_10pct"].min())` to `{python} pct(rec3["recall_top_10pct"].max())` of 3 year converters, and `{python} pct(rec5["recall_top_10pct"][0])` of 5 year converters. Even among never-major donors it reaches `{python} pct(rec12["never_major_recall_top_10pct"].min())` to `{python} pct(rec12["never_major_recall_top_10pct"].max())` for 12 months.

This changes how success should be defined:

- **The 25% target is too low.** A ranking a staff member could build in a spreadsheet already clears it by a wide margin, so meeting it would not show that the model adds anything.
- **The top 10% is larger than staff can work.** Ten percent of about `{python} n(round(recent_12["eligible"].mean(), -3))` eligible donors is about `{python} n(round(recent_12["eligible"].mean() * 0.1, -2))` people, while the cultivation program's capacity is 1,000 donors a year (8 portfolios of 125). Recall at 1,000 is a more realistic measure, and the simple ranking already gets `{python} pct(rec12["recall_top_1000"].min())` to `{python} pct(rec12["recall_top_1000"].max())` there for 12 months.
- **The baseline to beat is prior-year giving, not random selection.** The recency, frequency, and value baseline in the problem statement includes giving amount, so it should do at least roughly as well as this ranking. The model's value should be shown as lift over it, especially for never-major donors and the longer windows, where the simple ranking does worse.

These points are carried into the revisions section at the end of the notebook.

### Number of Backtest Cohorts

```{python}
#| label: cohort-counts
# number of cohorts available for each outcome window, with and without solicitation and Passport data

cohort_counts = pl.DataFrame([
    {
        "outcome": WINDOWS[w],
        "last_cohort": LAST_FY - w,
        "cohorts_giving_history_only": LAST_FY - w - 1999 + 1,
        "cohorts_with_solicitation_and_passport": max(0, LAST_FY - w - 2021 + 1),
    }
    for w in WINDOWS
])
show(cohort_counts, caption="Backtest cohorts available for each outcome window")
```

With giving history alone there are plenty of cohorts for every window. Once solicitation and Passport features are included, which only start in FY2021, the 12 month outcome has 5 cohorts, the 3 year outcome has 3, and the 5 year outcome has only one. The problem statement allows for this: if the data spans too few years, the 12 month window becomes the tested outcome and the 3 to 5 year window is reported as a projection. A reasonable plan is to test the 12 month and 3 year outcomes with full features, and to check the 5 year outcome with giving history only, where there are enough cohorts.

### Option D Check on Conversion

```{python}
#| label: option-d-conversion
# rebuild the cohorts from the option D panel and compare counts with option A

cohorts_d = build_cohorts(panel_d)
rates_a = cohorts.group_by("window", "t").agg(eligible_a=pl.len(), converters_a=pl.col("converted").sum())
rates_d = cohorts_d.group_by("window", "t").agg(eligible_d=pl.len(), converters_d=pl.col("converted").sum())
ad = rates_a.join(rates_d, on=["window", "t"])
conv_diff_max = ad.select((pl.col("converters_a") - pl.col("converters_d")).abs().max()).item()
conv_diff_recent = ad.filter(pl.col("t") >= 2021).select(
    (pl.col("converters_a") - pl.col("converters_d")).abs().max() + (pl.col("eligible_a") - pl.col("eligible_d")).abs().max()
).item()
```

Dropping spouse-shared legacy gifts changes the number of converters in any cohort by at most `{python} n(conv_diff_max)`, and `{python} "does not change any count" if conv_diff_recent == 0 else "changes counts slightly"` for cohorts from FY2021 on. The choice of option A is confirmed.

### Summary for Modeling

- The 12 month conversion rate is about `{python} pct(r12["rate"], 2)`, roughly `{python} n(recent_12["converters"].mean())` converters a year. This is an extremely imbalanced target, so models should be compared on ranking measures (recall and precision at a fixed list size, lift) and not on accuracy.
- Half of converters are former major donors who convert at about `{python} pct(r12_former["rate"], 0)` a year. Results should be reported separately for never-major donors.
- About nine in ten new major donors gave in the prior year, so the eligibility rule loses little.
- Prior-year giving alone beats the 25% target several times over. The target and the list size should be revised, and the main comparison should be against a prior-year giving or RFV baseline.
- The 12 month and 3 year outcomes can be backtested with all features. The 5 year outcome can only be backtested with giving history.

## Giving Behavior and Conversion

This section looks at which parts of a donor's giving history come before a conversion, and builds the recency, frequency, and value (RFV) baseline promised in the problem statement. Every feature is measured at the end of FY t using only gifts made through FY t, so nothing here uses information from the outcome year. The analysis uses the five Unite-era cohorts (FY2021 to FY2025) and the 12 month outcome, and reports rates for all eligible donors and for never-major donors separately.

### Features at the Prediction Date

```{python}
#| label: features

import datetime as dt

# every individual gift with its date, used for recency
gifts = pl.concat([
    pay_clean.filter(~pl.col("donor_id").is_in(ORG_IDS))
    .select(constituent_id=pl.col("donor_id"), date=pl.col("credit_date"), amount=pl.col("payment_amount")),
    sc_clean.select(constituent_id=pl.col("soft_credit_constituent_id"), date=pl.col("credit_date"), amount=pl.col("credit_amount")),
    ta_clean.select(constituent_id=pl.col("constituent_id_1"), date=pl.col("gift_date"), amount=pl.col("payment_amount")),
])

# Unite gift type labels and recurring payment counts by person and fiscal year
gift_labels = (
    pay_clean.filter(~pl.col("donor_id").is_in(ORG_IDS))
    .group_by(constituent_id=pl.col("donor_id"), fy=fiscal_year("credit_date"))
    .agg(
        upgrade_gift=(pl.col("gift_type") == "Upgrade").any(),
        additional_gift=(pl.col("gift_type") == "Additional").any(),
        recurring_payments=(pl.col("pledge_gift_type") == "Recurring").sum(),
    )
)
first_gift_fy = panel.group_by("constituent_id").agg(first_fy=pl.col("fy").min())

def features(t):
    # one row per eligible donor at the end of FY t, using only data through FY t
    end = dt.date(t, 6, 30)
    eligible = cohorts.filter((pl.col("t") == t) & (pl.col("window") == 1)).select(
        "constituent_id", "t", "prior_total", "former_major", "converted"
    )
    this_year = panel.filter(pl.col("fy") == t).select("constituent_id", "recurring_amt", "soft_amt")
    last_year = panel.filter(pl.col("fy") == t - 1).select("constituent_id", prev_total=pl.col("total"))
    history = panel.filter(pl.col("fy") <= t).group_by("constituent_id").agg(
        years_last5=pl.col("fy").filter(pl.col("fy") >= t - 4).n_unique(),
        soft_before=(pl.col("soft_amt").filter(pl.col("fy") < t) > 0).any(),
    )
    last_gift = gifts.filter(pl.col("date") <= end).group_by("constituent_id").agg(last_gift=pl.col("date").max())
    return (
        eligible.join(this_year, on="constituent_id", how="left")
        .join(last_year, on="constituent_id", how="left")
        .join(history, on="constituent_id", how="left")
        .join(last_gift, on="constituent_id", how="left")
        .join(first_gift_fy, on="constituent_id", how="left")
        .join(gift_labels.filter(pl.col("fy") == t).drop("fy"), on="constituent_id", how="left")
        .with_columns(
            recency_days=(pl.lit(end) - pl.col("last_gift")).dt.total_days(),
            tenure_years=pl.col("t") - pl.col("first_fy") + 1,
            prev_total=pl.col("prev_total").fill_null(0),
            monthly_amount=pl.when(pl.col("recurring_payments") > 0)
            .then(pl.col("recurring_amt") / pl.col("recurring_payments")),
            upgrade_gift=pl.col("upgrade_gift").fill_null(False),
            additional_gift=pl.col("additional_gift").fill_null(False),
            soft_this_year=pl.col("soft_amt") > 0,
        )
    )

feat = pl.concat([features(t) for t in range(2021, LAST_FY)])
base_all = feat["converted"].mean()
base_never = feat.filter(~pl.col("former_major"))["converted"].mean()
```

### Signals From Giving History

The table and plot below show the 12 month conversion rate for each level of several features, along with its lift over the base rate (`{python} pct(base_all, 3)` for all eligible donors and `{python} pct(base_never, 3)` for never-major donors).

```{python}
#| label: feature-signals

def change_label():
    return (
        pl.when(pl.col("prev_total") == 0).then(pl.lit("no gift last year"))
        .when(pl.col("prior_total") > pl.col("prev_total")).then(pl.lit("gave more than last year"))
        .when(pl.col("prior_total") < pl.col("prev_total")).then(pl.lit("gave less than last year"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("gave the same"))
    )

signal_specs = [
    ("Years given, last 5", pl.col("years_last5").cast(pl.String) + pl.lit(" of 5")),
    ("Years since first gift", pl.col("tenure_years").cut([1, 3, 10], labels=["1", "2 to 3", "4 to 10", "over 10"])),
    ("Change from last year", change_label()),
    ("Upgrade gift in FY t", pl.when(pl.col("upgrade_gift")).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no"))),
    ("Additional gift in FY t", pl.when(pl.col("additional_gift")).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no"))),
    ("Monthly sustainer amount", pl.when(pl.col("monthly_amount").is_null()).then(pl.lit("not a sustainer"))
        .when(pl.col("monthly_amount") <= 10).then(pl.lit("$10 or less"))
        .when(pl.col("monthly_amount") <= 25).then(pl.lit("$11 to $25"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("over $25"))),
    ("Soft credit before FY t", pl.when(pl.col("soft_before")).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no"))),
    ("Soft credit in FY t", pl.when(pl.col("soft_this_year")).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no"))),
    ("Days since last gift", pl.col("recency_days").cut([30, 90, 180], labels=["30 or less", "31 to 90", "91 to 180", "over 180"])),
]

def signal_rates(df, base):
    out = []
    for name, expr in signal_specs:
        out.append(
            df.with_columns(level=expr.cast(pl.String))
            .group_by("level").agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
            .with_columns(feature=pl.lit(name), rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
            .with_columns(lift=pl.col("rate") / base)
        )
    return pl.concat(out)

sig_all = signal_rates(feat, base_all)
sig_never = signal_rates(feat.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), base_never)
signals = (
    sig_all.join(sig_never.select("feature", "level", never_rate="rate", never_lift="lift"), on=["feature", "level"], how="left")
    .select("feature", "level", "eligible", "converters", "rate", "lift", "never_rate", "never_lift")
    .sort("feature", "level")
)

def sig(feature, level, col="rate"):
    return signals.filter((pl.col("feature") == feature) & (pl.col("level") == level))[col][0]

# share of monthly sustainers in the 31 to 90 day recency band
sust_31_90 = feat.filter(pl.col("recency_days").is_between(31, 90))["recurring_amt"].gt(0).mean()

show(signals.with_columns(pl.col("lift", "never_lift").round(2)), pct_cols=["rate", "never_rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="12 month conversion rate and lift by feature level")
```

```{python}
#| label: lift-plot
#| fig-height: 7

lift_long = pl.concat([
    sig_all.select("feature", "level", "lift", group=pl.lit("All eligible")),
    sig_never.select("feature", "level", "lift", group=pl.lit("Never major")),
]).filter(pl.col("lift") > 0).with_columns(
    # escape dollar signs so matplotlib does not read them as math
    label=(pl.col("feature") + ": " + pl.col("level")).str.replace_all("$", r"\$", literal=True)
)

(
    ggplot(lift_long.to_pandas(), aes("lift", "label", color="group"))
    + geom_vline(xintercept=1, linetype="dashed", color="grey")
    + geom_point(size=2.5)
    + scale_x_log10()
    + labs(x="Lift over the base rate (log scale)", y="", color="",
           title="Conversion lift by feature level",
           subtitle="12 month outcome, FY2021 to FY2025 cohorts")
    + theme(figure_size=(8, 7))
)
```

Several parts of giving history separate future major donors from everyone else:

- **Consistency.** Donors who gave in all five of the last five years convert at `{python} pct(sig("Years given, last 5", "5 of 5"), 2)`, compared with `{python} pct(sig("Years given, last 5", "1 of 5"), 2)` for donors who gave in only one. Longer giving histories show the same pattern, and first-year donors almost never convert.
- **Direction of change.** Among never-major donors, those who gave more than the year before convert at `{python} pct(sig("Change from last year", "gave more than last year", "never_rate"), 2)`, about `{python} f'{sig("Change from last year", "gave more than last year", "never_lift"):.1f}'` times the base rate, while those who gave less convert at `{python} pct(sig("Change from last year", "gave less than last year", "never_rate"), 3)`.
- **Upgrade gifts.** A gift labeled "Upgrade" in FY t raises the 12 month rate to `{python} pct(sig("Upgrade gift in FY t", "yes"), 2)`, roughly `{python} f'{sig("Upgrade gift in FY t", "yes", "lift"):.0f}'` times the base rate, and the effect holds for never-major donors. Because the label is attached to a gift in FY t, it is known at the prediction date and can be used.
- **Soft credits in an earlier year.** Donors with a soft credit before FY t convert at `{python} pct(sig("Soft credit before FY t", "yes"), 2)`, compared with `{python} pct(sig("Soft credit before FY t", "no"), 3)` for those without one.
- **Sustainers convert less.** Monthly sustainers convert at a lower rate than donors who are not on a monthly plan, and none of the `{python} n(signals.filter((pl.col("feature") == "Monthly sustainer amount") & (pl.col("level") == "over $25"))["eligible"][0])` eligible donor-years giving over $25 a month converted. Monthly giving seems to be a separate path from major giving, not a step toward it.
- **Recency is mixed.** Donors whose last gift came within 30 days of year end convert most often, but the next band (31 to 90 days) converts less often than donors whose last gift was more than 90 days before year end. Monthly sustainers make up `{python} pct(sust_31_90)` of that middle band, so recency is partly a stand-in for sustainer status here.

### Soft Credit Timing

Soft credits were tied closely to major giving in the panel section, so the timing matters. A soft credit in the same year a donor becomes major is part of the outcome, not a predictor of it.

```{python}
#| label: soft-timing

converters_12 = feat.filter(pl.col("converted")).select("constituent_id", "t", soft_before_or_t=pl.col("soft_before") | pl.col("soft_this_year"), soft_t=pl.col("soft_this_year"))
conversion_year_soft = panel.select("constituent_id", t=pl.col("fy") - 1, soft_conversion_year=pl.col("soft_amt") > 0)
soft_timing = converters_12.join(conversion_year_soft, on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
soft_in_t = soft_timing["soft_t"].mean()
soft_in_conv = soft_timing["soft_conversion_year"].mean()
soft_new_in_conv = (soft_timing["soft_conversion_year"] & ~soft_timing["soft_before_or_t"]).mean()
```

Among 12 month converters, `{python} pct(soft_in_conv)` have a soft credit in the year they convert, but only `{python} pct(soft_in_t)` had one in FY t, and `{python} pct(soft_new_in_conv)` received their first soft credit in the conversion year itself. So most major giving arrives through a soft credit in the same year, often the donor's first. For modeling:

- Soft credits from FY t and earlier are fair features and carry real signal.
- Soft credits from the outcome year must never be used, and any feature built from "lifetime" soft credits has to be cut off at the prediction date.
- Because `{python} pct(soft_new_in_conv)` of converters have no soft credit before the conversion year, the model will have to find a large share of them through other signals.

### Recency, Frequency, and Value Baseline

The problem statement compares the model against an RFV baseline. I built the standard version: each eligible donor gets a 1 to 5 score on each part, and the three scores are added (3 to 15).

- **Recency:** days from the last gift to the end of FY t, split into quintiles (most recent = 5).
- **Frequency:** number of fiscal years with a gift in the last five (1 to 5).
- **Value:** total giving in FY t, split into quintiles (highest = 5).

Quintiles are computed within each cohort. The table compares this score with the simpler ranking by prior-year total from the previous section, using recall in the top 10%, recall and precision in the top 1,000 (about the size of the cultivation program), and lift at 1,000. Ties at the cutoff are handled the same way as before.

```{python}
#| label: rfv

def quintile(col, descending=False):
    # 1 to 5 score from the within-cohort percentile rank, with ties sharing a rank
    pct_rank = pl.col(col).rank("average", descending=descending) / pl.len()
    return (pct_rank * 5).ceil().clip(1, 5).cast(pl.Int32).over("t")

scored = feat.with_columns(
    r_score=quintile("recency_days", descending=True),
    f_score=pl.col("years_last5").cast(pl.Int32),
    v_score=quintile("prior_total"),
).with_columns(rfv=pl.col("r_score") + pl.col("f_score") + pl.col("v_score"))

def top_k(df, col, k):
    # expected recall and precision in the top k by col, random order inside ties
    df = df.sort(col, descending=True)
    cut = df[col][k - 1]
    above = df.filter(pl.col(col) > cut)
    tied = df.filter(pl.col(col) == cut)
    hits = above["converted"].sum() + tied["converted"].sum() * (k - above.height) / tied.height
    return hits / df["converted"].sum(), hits / k

baseline_rows = []
for (t,), d in scored.group_by("t"):
    for group, dd in [("all eligible", d), ("never major", d.filter(~pl.col("former_major")))]:
        for name, col in [("prior-year total", "prior_total"), ("RFV score", "rfv")]:
            r10, _ = top_k(dd, col, round(dd.height * 0.10))
            r1k, p1k = top_k(dd, col, 1000)
            baseline_rows.append({
                "group": group, "baseline": name, "cohort": t,
                "recall_top_10pct": r10, "recall_top_1000": r1k, "precision_top_1000": p1k,
                "lift_top_1000": p1k / dd["converted"].mean(),
            })
baselines = pl.DataFrame(baseline_rows)
baseline_summary = (
    baselines.group_by("group", "baseline")
    .agg(pl.col("recall_top_10pct", "recall_top_1000", "precision_top_1000", "lift_top_1000").mean())
    .sort("group", "baseline")
)

def bl(group, baseline, col):
    return baseline_summary.filter((pl.col("group") == group) & (pl.col("baseline") == baseline))[col][0]

v5_floor = scored.filter(pl.col("v_score") == 5)["prior_total"].min()

# conversion and sustainer share by recency score
by_r = scored.group_by("r_score").agg(
    rate=pl.col("converted").mean(), sustainer_share=(pl.col("recurring_amt") > 0).mean()
).sort("r_score")
r_rate = dict(zip(by_r["r_score"], by_r["rate"]))
r_sust_mid = scored.filter(pl.col("r_score").is_in([3, 4]))["recurring_amt"].gt(0).mean()
share_600 = feat.filter(pl.col("prior_total").is_between(500, 750, closed="right")).select((pl.col("prior_total") == 600).mean()).item()

show(baseline_summary.with_columns(pl.col("lift_top_1000").round(1)),
     pct_cols=["recall_top_10pct", "recall_top_1000", "precision_top_1000"], caption="Prior-year giving compared with the RFV score as baselines")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Baseline results by cohort

```{python}
#| label: rfv-by-cohort
show(baselines.sort("group", "baseline", "cohort").with_columns(pl.col("lift_top_1000").round(1)),
     pct_cols=["recall_top_10pct", "recall_top_1000", "precision_top_1000"], caption="Baseline results by cohort")
```
:::

The standard RFV score is clearly weaker than ranking by prior-year total. Averaged over the five cohorts, RFV puts `{python} pct(bl("all eligible", "RFV score", "recall_top_10pct"))` of converters in the top 10% and `{python} pct(bl("all eligible", "RFV score", "recall_top_1000"))` in the top 1,000, while prior-year total puts `{python} pct(bl("all eligible", "prior-year total", "recall_top_10pct"))` and `{python} pct(bl("all eligible", "prior-year total", "recall_top_1000"))` there. For never-major donors the gap is similar (`{python} pct(bl("never major", "RFV score", "recall_top_1000"))` versus `{python} pct(bl("never major", "prior-year total", "recall_top_1000"))` in the top 1,000).

There are two reasons. First, the top value quintile starts at `{python} usd(v5_floor)`, so it lumps the donors who matter most together with many who rarely convert. That matters because the $501 to $750 group that produces most converters is almost all donors who gave exactly $600 (`{python} pct(share_600)` of that group). Second, conversion does not rise steadily with the recency score. Donors with the most recent gifts (score 5) convert at `{python} pct(r_rate[5], 2)`, but the middle scores 3 and 4, which are `{python} pct(r_sust_mid)` monthly sustainers, convert at only `{python} pct(r_rate[3], 3)` and `{python} pct(r_rate[4], 3)`, below even the least recent group (`{python} pct(r_rate[1], 2)`). Adding recency as if more recent were always better pushes many sustainers up the list. Both points suggest the model should use giving amounts directly instead of coarse bins, and should let recency interact with sustainer status instead of treating it as a straight line.

For judging the model, I would use both baselines as planned, but treat prior-year total as the one to beat because it is stronger. Its precision in the top 1,000 averages `{python} pct(bl("all eligible", "prior-year total", "precision_top_1000"))`, about `{python} f'{bl("all eligible", "prior-year total", "lift_top_1000"):.0f}'` times the base rate, which sets a high but fair bar.

### Summary for Modeling

- **Useful features, all measured through FY t:** prior-year total, former major status, years given in the last five, years since first gift, change from the previous year, an upgrade gift in FY t, soft credits before or in FY t, and monthly sustainer status and amount.
- **Leakage rules:** no soft credits, gift labels, or totals from the outcome years, and no lifetime figures that run past the prediction date.
- **Baselines:** RFV is weaker than prior-year total alone. The model should be compared with both, and success should be judged against prior-year total.
- **Sustainers** are a large group with low conversion, so the model should not treat recent monthly giving as a sign of major potential.

## Solicitation History

The campaign members table records who was solicited under which marketing code in each fiscal year, and whether they responded with a payment on that code in the same year. The only campaign attribute that varies is communication method, so the analysis focuses on how much each donor is solicited, how often they respond, and through which channels.

### Solicitation Volume Over Time

```{python}
#| label: solicitation-volume
# attach communication method to each solicitation and summarize volume by year and channel

solicit = (
    cm.join(cc.select("marketing_code", "communication_method"), on="marketing_code", how="left")
    .with_columns(fy=fiscal_year("campaign_start_date"),
                  never_donor=pl.col("constituent_id").str.starts_with("SYN-ND"))
)

sol_by_year = (
    solicit.group_by("fy")
    .agg(
        solicitations=pl.len(),
        people_solicited=pl.col("constituent_id").n_unique(),
        never_donors_solicited=pl.col("constituent_id").filter(pl.col("never_donor")).n_unique(),
        marketing_codes=pl.col("marketing_code").n_unique(),
        response_rate=pl.col("responded").mean(),
    )
    .sort("fy")
)
method_share = (
    solicit.group_by("communication_method").agg(solicitations=pl.len())
    .with_columns(share=pl.col("solicitations") / pl.col("solicitations").sum())
    .sort("solicitations", descending=True)
)
legacy_method_share = method_share.filter(pl.col("communication_method") == "Legacy")["share"][0]
s21 = sol_by_year.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2021).row(0, named=True)
s24 = sol_by_year.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2024).row(0, named=True)
s25 = sol_by_year.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2025).row(0, named=True)
s26 = sol_by_year.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2026).row(0, named=True)

show(sol_by_year, pct_cols=["response_rate"], caption="Solicitation volume and response rate by fiscal year")
```

```{python}
#| label: method-share
show(method_share, pct_cols=["share"], caption="Solicitations by communication method")
```

Solicitation grew quickly over the Unite years. PBS Utah solicited `{python} n(s21["people_solicited"])` people in FY2021 and `{python} n(s26["people_solicited"])` in FY2026, and the number of never-donors solicited grew from `{python} n(s21["never_donors_solicited"])` to `{python} n(s26["never_donors_solicited"])`. FY2025 is the exception, with `{python} n(s25["people_solicited"])` people solicited after `{python} n(s24["people_solicited"])` in FY2024. As outreach widened, the response rate per solicitation fell from `{python} pct(s21["response_rate"])` to `{python} pct(s26["response_rate"])`. Because these swings come from PBS Utah's own mailing decisions, a donor's solicitation count partly reflects which lists they were on that year and not only their own behavior.

On communication method, `{python} pct(legacy_method_share)` of solicitation rows have the method "Legacy," a value that is not listed for this field in the reference dictionary, the same as the "Legacy" tender type. It is added to the data concerns at the top. In-person and phone solicitations are rare.

### Solicitation and Conversion

For each eligible donor, I counted solicitations, distinct marketing codes, and responses in FY t, plus whether they received any solicitation by mail, email, digital, phone, or in person. These are joined to the same FY2021 to FY2025 cohorts used in the previous section.

```{python}
#| label: solicitation-features
# solicitation counts, responses, and channels per eligible donor in FY t, then banded for comparison

sol_py = solicit.group_by("constituent_id", "fy").agg(
    solicitations=pl.len(),
    responses=pl.col("responded").sum(),
    **{f"by_{m.lower().replace('-', '_')}": (pl.col("communication_method") == m).any()
       for m in ["Mail", "Email", "Digital", "Phone", "In-Person"]},
)
feat_sol = (
    feat.join(sol_py.rename({"fy": "t"}), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("solicitations", "responses").fill_null(0),
                  pl.col("^by_.*$").fill_null(False))
)
share_solicited = (feat_sol["solicitations"] > 0).mean()
rho_sol_prior = feat_sol.select(pl.corr("solicitations", "prior_total", method="spearman")).item()

SOL_LABELS = ["none", "1 to 5", "6 to 10", "11 to 20", "21 to 40", "over 40"]
RESP_LABELS = ["none", "1", "2", "3 or more"]
feat_sol = feat_sol.with_columns(
    sol_band=pl.col("solicitations").cut([0, 5, 10, 20, 40], labels=SOL_LABELS).cast(pl.Enum(SOL_LABELS)),
    resp_band=pl.col("responses").cut([0, 1, 2], labels=RESP_LABELS).cast(pl.Enum(RESP_LABELS)),
    prior_band=pl.col("prior_total").cut([240, 500], labels=["$240 or less", "$241 to $500", "over $500"]),
)

def rate_table(by):
    return (
        feat_sol.group_by(by).agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum(),
                                  median_prior_total=pl.col("prior_total").median())
        .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
        .sort(by)
    )

sol_rates = rate_table("sol_band")
resp_rates = rate_table("resp_band")
show(sol_rates, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="12 month conversion by number of solicitations in FY t")
```

```{python}
#| label: response-rates
show(resp_rates, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="12 month conversion by number of responses in FY t")
```

`{python} pct(share_solicited)` of eligible donors were solicited at least once in FY t, so being solicited at all does not separate anyone. The number of solicitations barely matters: conversion stays between `{python} pct(sol_rates["rate"].min(), 2)` and `{python} pct(sol_rates["rate"].max(), 2)` across solicitation bands, and the rank correlation between solicitations and prior-year giving is only `{python} f"{rho_sol_prior:.2f}"`. Responses look more useful at first, since donors who responded to more solicitations convert more often. But their median prior-year giving also rises with the number of responses, so part of that pattern is just giving level showing up again.

The table below checks both features inside bands of prior-year giving, to see whether they add anything once giving is held roughly constant.

```{python}
#| label: solicitation-within-band
# conversion by solicitation volume and by responses, inside bands of prior-year giving

within = (
    feat_sol.group_by("prior_band", "sol_band")
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
    .sort("prior_band", "sol_band")
)
top_within = within.filter((pl.col("prior_band") == "over $500") & (pl.col("sol_band") != "none"))
resp_within = (
    feat_sol.group_by("prior_band", "resp_band")
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
    .sort("prior_band", "resp_band")
)
top_resp = resp_within.filter(pl.col("prior_band") == "over $500")

show(within, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=2, caption="Conversion by solicitation volume within prior-year giving bands")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Responses within prior-year giving bands

```{python}
#| label: responses-within-band
show(resp_within, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=2, caption="Conversion by responses within prior-year giving bands")
```
:::

Once prior-year giving is held constant, solicitation volume adds little. Among donors who gave over $500 and were solicited at least once, conversion stays between `{python} pct(top_within["rate"].min())` and `{python} pct(top_within["rate"].max())` regardless of how many solicitations they received. In the $241 to $500 band, donors with more than ten solicitations convert a bit more often than those with fewer, but the counts are small. Responses show the same thing: in the over $500 band, donors with no response convert at `{python} pct(top_resp.filter(pl.col("resp_band") == "none")["rate"][0])` and donors with one at `{python} pct(top_resp.filter(pl.col("resp_band") == "1")["rate"][0])`, so the overall response pattern mostly reflects giving level.

### Communication Channel

```{python}
#| label: channel-rates
# conversion for donors who did or did not receive each communication channel in FY t

channel_rates = pl.concat([
    feat_sol.group_by(pl.col(f"by_{c}").alias("received"))
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(channel=pl.lit(label), rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
    for c, label in [("mail", "Mail"), ("email", "Email"), ("digital", "Digital"), ("phone", "Phone"), ("in_person", "In-Person")]
]).select("channel", "received", "eligible", "converters", "rate").sort("channel", "received")
inperson_conv = channel_rates.filter((pl.col("channel") == "In-Person") & pl.col("received"))["converters"][0]

show(channel_rates, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Conversion for donors who did or did not receive each channel")
```

No channel stands out. Donors who received mail, email, digital, or phone solicitations convert at rates close to those who did not, and in-person solicitation, which might be expected to mark major gift prospects, is linked to only `{python} n(inperson_conv)` converters. Channel indicators can go into the model, but I would not expect much from them.

### Solicitations in the Outcome Year

```{python}
#| label: outcome-year-solicitations
# average solicitations in FY t and in the outcome year, for converters and non-converters

next_year_sol = sol_py.select("constituent_id", t=pl.col("fy") - 1, next_year_solicitations=pl.col("solicitations"))
outcome_sol = (
    feat_sol.join(next_year_sol, on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("next_year_solicitations").fill_null(0))
    .group_by("converted")
    .agg(solicitations_fy_t=pl.col("solicitations").mean(), solicitations_outcome_year=pl.col("next_year_solicitations").mean())
    .sort("converted")
)
osol = {r["converted"]: r for r in outcome_sol.iter_rows(named=True)}

show(outcome_sol, caption="Average solicitations in FY t and in the outcome year")
```

In FY t, converters and non-converters receive a similar number of solicitations (`{python} f'{osol[True]["solicitations_fy_t"]:.1f}'` versus `{python} f'{osol[False]["solicitations_fy_t"]:.1f}'` on average). In the outcome year the gap opens up: converters receive `{python} f'{osol[True]["solicitations_outcome_year"]:.1f}'` solicitations and non-converters `{python} f'{osol[False]["solicitations_outcome_year"]:.1f}'`. One possible reason is that donors are taken off mass appeals once they give at the major level, though the data does not show why. Either way, solicitation counts from the outcome year depend on the outcome and must not be used as features.

### Summary for Modeling

- Nearly every eligible donor is solicited, and solicitation volume adds little once prior-year giving is known. It also reflects PBS Utah's mailing decisions, which changed a lot from year to year.
- Responses mostly repeat the giving signal. They can be included, but should not be expected to add much.
- No communication channel is a strong signal.
- Solicitations from the outcome year must be excluded, since converters are solicited much less in the year they give at the major level.
- Because solicitation features add little, the model will lose little if they are left out for the 5 year outcome, where only giving history can be used.

## Passport Viewing

The Passport table summarizes each constituent's streaming by fiscal year and genre: how many distinct titles they watched and the average share of each title they finished. A constituent-year only has rows if something was watched, so a missing year can mean no linked Passport account, no consent to share viewing, or no viewing. I treat a missing year as "no viewing record" and keep a separate flag for it, so the model can tell a missing record apart from light viewing.

### Who Shows Up in the Viewing Data

```{python}
#| label: passport-coverage
# viewing summarized per person and year, with the share who gave that year and who view again next year

view_py = pv.group_by("constituent_id", "fiscal_year").agg(
    titles=pl.col("titles_viewed").sum(),
    genres=pl.len(),
    share_watched=(pl.col("mean_percent_watched") * pl.col("titles_viewed")).sum() / pl.col("titles_viewed").sum(),
    top_genre=pl.col("genre").sort_by("titles_viewed", descending=True).first(),
).rename({"fiscal_year": "fy"})

donor_years_flag = panel.select("constituent_id", "fy", gave_that_year=pl.lit(True))
viewer_years = sorted(view_py["fy"].unique().to_list())

def viewer_retention(fy):
    this_year = view_py.filter(pl.col("fy") == fy)["constituent_id"]
    next_year = view_py.filter(pl.col("fy") == fy + 1)["constituent_id"]
    return this_year.is_in(next_year.implode()).mean() if next_year.len() else None

viewers_by_year = (
    view_py.join(donor_years_flag, on=["constituent_id", "fy"], how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("gave_that_year").fill_null(False),
                  never_donor=pl.col("constituent_id").str.starts_with("SYN-ND"))
    .group_by("fy")
    .agg(viewers=pl.len(), median_titles=pl.col("titles").median(),
         share_gave_that_year=pl.col("gave_that_year").mean(), share_never_donors=pl.col("never_donor").mean())
    .sort("fy")
    .with_columns(viewing_again_next_year=pl.col("fy").map_elements(viewer_retention, return_dtype=pl.Float64))
)
vret = viewers_by_year.filter(pl.col("viewing_again_next_year").is_not_null())["viewing_again_next_year"]
donor_ret_unite = retention_df.filter(pl.col("fy") >= 2021)["retention"]
v25 = viewers_by_year.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2025).row(0, named=True)
v26 = viewers_by_year.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2026).row(0, named=True)

show(viewers_by_year, pct_cols=["share_gave_that_year", "share_never_donors", "viewing_again_next_year"], caption="Passport viewers by year and how often viewing carries over")
```

About 20,000 people have viewing records each year, rising to `{python} n(v26["viewers"])` in FY2026 from `{python} n(v25["viewers"])` in FY2025. Most viewers gave in the same year, which fits Passport being a member benefit, and the share rises to `{python} pct(v26["share_gave_that_year"])` in FY2026. The median viewer watched about `{python} n(viewers_by_year["median_titles"].median())` titles in a year.

The surprising part is how little viewing carries over. Only `{python} pct(vret.min())` to `{python} pct(vret.max())` of one year's viewers have viewing records the next year, while `{python} pct(donor_ret_unite.min())` to `{python} pct(donor_ret_unite.max())` of donors give again the next year. If Passport access comes with membership, I would expect viewing to be at least as persistent as giving. This is listed in the data concerns at the top.

### Viewing and Conversion

```{python}
#| label: passport-features
# viewing features for eligible donors in FY t, and conversion by viewing level and genre

ever_viewed = pv.select("constituent_id", "fiscal_year").unique()
feat_pv = feat.join(view_py.rename({"fy": "t"}), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left").with_columns(
    viewed_fy_t=pl.col("titles").is_not_null(),
    titles=pl.col("titles").fill_null(0),
)
viewed_by_t = (
    feat_pv.select("constituent_id", "t").join(ever_viewed, on="constituent_id")
    .filter(pl.col("fiscal_year") <= pl.col("t")).select("constituent_id", "t").unique()
    .with_columns(viewed_by_t=pl.lit(True))
)
feat_pv = feat_pv.join(viewed_by_t, on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left").with_columns(pl.col("viewed_by_t").fill_null(False))

share_viewed_t = feat_pv["viewed_fy_t"].mean()
share_viewed_ever = feat_pv["viewed_by_t"].mean()
rho_titles_prior = feat_pv.filter(pl.col("viewed_fy_t")).select(pl.corr("titles", "prior_total", method="spearman")).item()

TITLE_LABELS = ["no viewing record", "1 to 5", "6 to 15", "16 to 40", "over 40"]
pv_levels = [
    ("Viewing record in FY t", pl.when(pl.col("viewed_fy_t")).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no"))),
    ("Titles viewed in FY t", pl.when(~pl.col("viewed_fy_t")).then(pl.lit("no viewing record"))
        .otherwise(pl.col("titles").cut([5, 15, 40], labels=TITLE_LABELS[1:]).cast(pl.String))),
    ("Most watched genre", pl.col("top_genre").fill_null("no viewing record")),
]
pv_rates = pl.concat([
    feat_pv.with_columns(level=expr).group_by("level")
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(feature=pl.lit(name), rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
    for name, expr in pv_levels
]).select("feature", "level", "eligible", "converters", "rate").sort("feature", "level")

def pvr(feature, level):
    return pv_rates.filter((pl.col("feature") == feature) & (pl.col("level") == level)).row(0, named=True)

show(pv_rates, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="12 month conversion by Passport viewing level and genre")
```

`{python} pct(share_viewed_t)` of eligible donors have a viewing record in FY t, and `{python} pct(share_viewed_ever)` have one in some year up to FY t. Viewers convert at `{python} pct(pvr("Viewing record in FY t", "yes")["rate"], 2)`, lower than donors without a viewing record (`{python} pct(pvr("Viewing record in FY t", "no")["rate"], 2)`). Among viewers, heavier viewing goes with somewhat higher conversion, but even the heaviest viewers convert less often than non-viewers. Most genres have too few converters to compare. News and Public Affairs has the highest rate, but it rests on only `{python} n(pvr("Most watched genre", "News and Public Affairs")["converters"])` converters.

Viewing is also almost unrelated to giving. Among eligible donors with a viewing record, the rank correlation between titles viewed and prior-year giving is `{python} f"{rho_titles_prior:.2f}"`. To see whether the lower rate for viewers is about viewing itself or about who views, the table below compares viewers and non-viewers within bands of prior-year giving.

```{python}
#| label: passport-within-band
# conversion for viewers and non-viewers inside bands of prior-year giving

pv_within = (
    feat_pv.with_columns(prior_band=pl.col("prior_total").cut([240, 500], labels=["$240 or less", "$241 to $500", "over $500"]),
                         viewing=pl.when(pl.col("viewed_fy_t")).then(pl.lit("viewer")).otherwise(pl.lit("no viewing record")))
    .group_by("prior_band", "viewing")
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
    .sort("prior_band", "viewing")
)
top_pv = {r["viewing"]: r for r in pv_within.filter(pl.col("prior_band") == "over $500").iter_rows(named=True)}
show(pv_within, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Conversion for viewers and non-viewers within prior-year giving bands")
```

Within each giving band, viewers and non-viewers convert at similar rates. In the over $500 band the rates are `{python} pct(top_pv["viewer"]["rate"])` for viewers and `{python} pct(top_pv["no viewing record"]["rate"])` for non-viewers. The overall gap comes from who views: only `{python} n(top_pv["viewer"]["eligible"])` of the `{python} n(top_pv["viewer"]["eligible"] + top_pv["no viewing record"]["eligible"])` eligible donors in that top band have a viewing record. So viewing does not seem to add information once giving is known.

### Summary for Modeling

- About half of eligible donors have a viewing record in a given year, so coverage is reasonable, but the missing years cannot be explained from the data. A "no viewing record" flag should go into the model alongside any viewing measures.
- Viewing shows little relationship with conversion once prior-year giving is held constant, and almost no relationship with giving itself. Passport features may add little, which also means losing them for the 5 year outcome costs little.
- Viewing data is not persistent from year to year, which is unusual enough to report. If the viewing records turn out to be incomplete and are corrected, the conclusions here could change. Either way, the problem statement's emphasis on viewing behavior should be revisited after modeling.

## Constituent Snapshot Fields

The constituents table has one row per person with fields measured at the end of the data (FY2026). These include PBS classifications (major donor class, annual giving group, sustainer flag), demographics, and three University of Utah dollar fields that the problem statement treats as capacity information. A snapshot field can only be used as a feature if its value at an earlier prediction date would have been the same, or can be rebuilt. The first question is therefore how each field relates to giving in FY2026 and earlier.

### What the Classification Fields Encode

```{python}
#| label: snapshot-status

# each person's PBS giving status at the snapshot, built from the panel
status = (
    con.filter(pl.col("constituent_id").str.starts_with("S0"))
    .select("constituent_id", "major_donor_class_pbs_utah", "annual_giving_group", "sustainer_pbs_utah",
            "lifetime_uofu_fundraising", "previous_fy_uofu_cash", "prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu")
    .join(panel.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2026).select("constituent_id", total_fy26=pl.col("total"), recurring_fy26=pl.col("recurring_amt")),
          on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .join(panel.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2025).select("constituent_id", total_fy25=pl.col("total")), on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .join(panel.group_by("constituent_id").agg(lifetime_pbs=pl.col("total").sum(),
                                               major_before_fy26=pl.col("major").filter(pl.col("fy") < 2026).any()),
          on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("total_fy26", "recurring_fy26", "total_fy25", "lifetime_pbs").fill_null(0),
                  pl.col("major_before_fy26").fill_null(False))
)

class_decode = (
    status.group_by(major_donor_class=pl.col("major_donor_class_pbs_utah").fill_null("(blank)"))
    .agg(constituents=pl.len(),
         major_in_fy26=(pl.col("total_fy26") >= 1200).mean(),
         major_before_fy26=pl.col("major_before_fy26").mean(),
         min_fy26_total=pl.col("total_fy26").min(), max_fy26_total=pl.col("total_fy26").max())
    .sort("constituents")
)
group_decode = (
    status.group_by("annual_giving_group")
    .agg(constituents=pl.len(),
         gave_in_fy26=(pl.col("total_fy26") > 0).mean(),
         min_fy26_total=pl.col("total_fy26").filter(pl.col("total_fy26") > 0).min(),
         max_fy26_total=pl.col("total_fy26").filter(pl.col("total_fy26") > 0).max())
    .sort("min_fy26_total", nulls_last=False)
)
sustainer_match = ((status["sustainer_pbs_utah"]) == (status["recurring_fy26"] > 0)).mean()

show(class_decode, pct_cols=["major_in_fy26", "major_before_fy26"], caption="Major donor class compared with FY2026 giving")
```

```{python}
#| label: group-decode
show(group_decode, pct_cols=["gave_in_fy26"], caption="Annual giving group compared with FY2026 giving")
```

All three PBS classifications can be rebuilt exactly from FY2026 giving:

- **Major donor class.** Broadcaster and Director are exactly the people who gave $1,200 or more in FY2026. Broadcasters gave exactly $1,200, and Directors gave $2,000 or more. Former means major in an earlier year but not in FY2026, and a blank means never major. The documented ranges ($1,000 to $4,999 for Broadcaster and $5,000 to $9,999 for Director) do not match, and the Patron and Lapsed values never appear.
- **Annual giving group.** The dictionary lists its meaning as unknown, but it lines up with FY2026 giving bands: ND means no gift in FY2026, and PD, LD, SL, and CD are increasing ranges of FY2026 giving, with CD starting at $1,200.
- **Sustainer flag.** It matches "had recurring payments in FY2026" for `{python} pct(sustainer_match)` of constituents.

Each of these fields describes the final year of the data, so for any earlier prediction date it carries information from the future. For the FY2025 cohort, whose outcome year is FY2026, the major donor class and annual giving group simply are the outcome. All three are dropped as features. The same information can be rebuilt for any year from the giving panel, and the earlier sections already do that with features like former major status and monthly sustainer amount.

### What the University of Utah Fields Encode

The problem statement lists University of Utah capacity information as an input. The three UofU dollar fields were compared with each person's PBS giving.

```{python}
#| label: uofu-decode

givers = status.filter(pl.col("lifetime_pbs") > 0)
uofu_checks = pl.DataFrame([
    {"field": "Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "compared_with": "lifetime PBS giving",
     "check": "correlation", "value": givers.select(pl.corr("lifetime_uofu_fundraising", "lifetime_pbs")).item()},
    {"field": "Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "compared_with": "lifetime PBS giving",
     "check": "share at least as large", "value": (givers["lifetime_uofu_fundraising"] >= givers["lifetime_pbs"]).mean()},
    {"field": "Previous FY UofU Cash", "compared_with": "FY2025 PBS giving",
     "check": "share where both are positive or both zero", "value": ((status["previous_fy_uofu_cash"] > 0) == (status["total_fy25"] > 0)).mean()},
    {"field": "Previous FY UofU Cash", "compared_with": "FY2025 PBS giving",
     "check": "share exactly equal", "value": (status["previous_fy_uofu_cash"] == status["total_fy25"]).mean()},
    {"field": "Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "compared_with": "sustainer flag",
     "check": "share where positive exactly when sustainer", "value": ((status["prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu"] > 0) == status["sustainer_pbs_utah"]).mean()},
    {"field": "Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "compared_with": "FY2026 recurring giving",
     "check": "share exactly equal", "value": (status["prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu"] == status["recurring_fy26"]).mean()},
])
uofu = {(r["field"], r["check"]): r["value"] for r in uofu_checks.iter_rows(named=True)}

# conversion by lifetime UofU amount, to show how strong the leak would look
feat_uofu = feat.join(con.select("constituent_id", "lifetime_uofu_fundraising"), on="constituent_id", how="left")
uofu_conv = (
    feat_uofu.with_columns(band=pl.col("lifetime_uofu_fundraising").cut([1000, 5000], labels=["$1,000 or less", "$1,001 to $5,000", "over $5,000"]))
    .group_by("band").agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"), share_of_converters=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("converters").sum())
    .sort("band")
)
uofu_top = uofu_conv.filter(pl.col("band") == "over $5,000").row(0, named=True)
uofu_low = uofu_conv.filter(pl.col("band") == "$1,000 or less").row(0, named=True)

show(uofu_checks.with_columns(value=pl.when(pl.col("check") == "correlation").then(pl.col("value").round(2).cast(pl.String))
                              .otherwise((pl.col("value") * 100).round(1).cast(pl.String) + "%")), caption="How the UofU dollar fields relate to PBS giving")
```

```{python}
#| label: uofu-conversion
show(uofu_conv, pct_cols=["rate", "share_of_converters"], pct_digits=2, caption="Conversion by lifetime UofU fundraising (a field that leaks the outcome)")
```

None of the three fields is independent of PBS giving:

- **Lifetime UofU Fundraising** has a correlation of `{python} f'{uofu[("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "correlation")]:.2f}'` with lifetime PBS giving and is at least as large as lifetime PBS giving for `{python} pct(uofu[("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "share at least as large")])` of donors. It looks like a total that includes PBS Utah giving through FY2026.
- **Previous FY UofU Cash** is positive exactly when the person gave to PBS in FY2025 (`{python} pct(uofu[("Previous FY UofU Cash", "share where both are positive or both zero")])` agreement) and equals their FY2025 PBS total for `{python} pct(uofu[("Previous FY UofU Cash", "share exactly equal")])` of constituents.
- **Prospect Committed Giving** is positive exactly when the sustainer flag is set (`{python} pct(uofu[("Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "share where positive exactly when sustainer")])` agreement) and equals FY2026 recurring giving for `{python} pct(uofu[("Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "share exactly equal")])`.

The lifetime field would look like an excellent predictor: eligible donors with more than $5,000 in lifetime UofU giving convert at `{python} pct(uofu_top["rate"])` and make up `{python} pct(uofu_top["share_of_converters"])` of converters, while those at $1,000 or less `{python} "never convert" if uofu_low["converters"] == 0 else "rarely convert"`. That strength comes from the field counting the outcome years. All three are dropped. This leaves the project without any information on giving capacity outside PBS Utah, which affects the problem statement's inputs and is listed in the data concerns at the top.

### Fields That Can Be Used

The remaining fields describe the person rather than their giving. Age can be shifted back to the prediction date (age in FY t = age in FY2026 minus 2026 + t), assuming the snapshot age is as of FY2026. Gender, state, constituent type, and having a spouse on file are assumed not to change.

```{python}
#| label: usable-snapshot

feat_demo = feat.join(
    con.select("constituent_id", "age", "gender", "address_state", "primary_constituent_type", "spouse_constituent_id"),
    on="constituent_id", how="left",
).with_columns(
    age_at_t=pl.col("age") - (2026 - pl.col("t")),
    utah=pl.col("address_state") == "UT",
    has_spouse=pl.col("spouse_constituent_id").is_not_null(),
)
AGE_LABELS = ["under 41", "41 to 55", "56 to 70", "71 to 85", "over 85"]
demo_specs = [
    ("Age at prediction date", pl.col("age_at_t").cut([40, 55, 70, 85], labels=AGE_LABELS).cast(pl.String)),
    ("Gender", pl.col("gender")),
    ("Lives in Utah", pl.when(pl.col("utah")).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no"))),
    ("Spouse on file", pl.when(pl.col("has_spouse")).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no"))),
    ("Constituent type", pl.col("primary_constituent_type")),
]
demo_rates = pl.concat([
    feat_demo.with_columns(level=expr).group_by("level")
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(feature=pl.lit(name), rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
    for name, expr in demo_specs
]).filter(pl.col("eligible") >= 500).select("feature", "level", "eligible", "converters", "rate").sort("feature", "level")

def dr(feature, level):
    return demo_rates.filter((pl.col("feature") == feature) & (pl.col("level") == level))["rate"][0]

# does age still matter once prior-year giving is held constant?
age_within = (
    feat_demo.filter(pl.col("prior_total") > 500)
    .group_by(age_71_plus=pl.col("age_at_t") > 70)
    .agg(eligible=pl.len(), converters=pl.col("converted").sum())
    .with_columns(rate=pl.col("converters") / pl.col("eligible"))
    .sort("age_71_plus")
)
aw = {r["age_71_plus"]: r["rate"] for r in age_within.iter_rows(named=True)}

# constituent type versus giving tenure
type_tenure = feat_demo.group_by("primary_constituent_type").agg(median_tenure=pl.col("tenure_years").median())
tt = dict(zip(type_tenure["primary_constituent_type"], type_tenure["median_tenure"]))

show(demo_rates, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="12 month conversion by usable constituent fields")
```

Levels with fewer than 500 eligible donor-years are left out of the table.

- **Age** has a clear pattern. Donors over 70 at the prediction date convert at about `{python} pct(dr("Age at prediction date", "71 to 85"), 2)`, compared with `{python} pct(dr("Age at prediction date", "under 41"), 2)` for donors 40 and under. The pattern holds among donors who gave over $500 in FY t (`{python} pct(aw[True])` for those over 70 versus `{python} pct(aw[False])` for younger donors), so age adds something beyond giving level.
- **Gender** matters mainly through the "Unknown" group, which converts at `{python} pct(dr("Gender", "Unknown"), 3)`, about a third of the rate for women and men. Unknown gender may mark thinner records, in which case it is more a data completeness signal than a demographic one.
- **State and spouse** make little difference.
- **Constituent type** shows "Friends" converting more often than "Donors" (`{python} pct(dr("Constituent type", "Friends"), 3)` versus `{python} pct(dr("Constituent type", "Donors"), 3)`). The type also tracks giving tenure (median `{python} n(tt["Friends"])` years for Friends and `{python} n(tt["Donors"])` for Donors), so it may be a snapshot label that changed over time. Whether to use it is a decision for the modeling plan.

### Summary for Modeling

- **Drop:** major donor class, annual giving group, sustainer flag, and all three UofU dollar fields. Each is rebuilt from giving through FY2026 and would leak the outcome.
- **Use:** age shifted to the prediction date, gender (with "Unknown" as its own level), and, with less expected value, state and spouse on file.
- **Decide:** constituent type, which may encode tenure or a label that changed after the prediction date.
- There is no usable outside measure of giving capacity, so the model has to rely on PBS giving history.

## Cultivation Program

From FY2022 to FY2025, each of eight officer portfolios selected 125 donors a year for possible cultivation. Within each portfolio, about three quarters of the selected donors were assigned for contact and the rest were randomly held out. The portfolios also adopted a cultivation program at different times. This setup matters for two reasons: contact may change who becomes a major donor, which affects the outcome the model learns from, and the random holdout gives a fair way to measure that effect.

### How the Program Was Run

```{python}
#| label: cultivation-setup

cult = (
    cu.rename({"synthetic_id": "constituent_id", "fiscal_year": "t"})
    .join(op.select("portfolio_id", "rollout_fy"), on="portfolio_id", how="left")
)
cult_summary = (
    cult.group_by("t")
    .agg(selected=pl.len(), contacted=pl.col("contacted").sum(), held_out=pl.col("holdout").sum(),
         in_adopting_portfolios=pl.col("program_adopted").sum())
    .sort("t")
)
adoption_matches_rollout = (cult["program_adopted"] == (cult["t"] >= cult["rollout_fy"].fill_null(9999))).mean()
times_selected = cult.group_by("constituent_id").agg(times=pl.len())["times"].value_counts().sort("times")
selected_once = times_selected.filter(pl.col("times") == 1)["count"][0]
selected_people = cult["constituent_id"].n_unique()

# timing: giving in the assignment year itself
cult_year = cult.join(panel.select("constituent_id", t=pl.col("fy"), total_t=pl.col("total")), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
gave_in_assignment_year = (cult_year["total_t"].fill_null(0) > 0).mean()
major_in_assignment_year = (cult_year["total_t"].fill_null(0) >= 1200).mean()

show(cult_summary, caption="Cultivation selections, contacts, and holdouts by year")
```

Each year 1,000 donors were selected, and the share assigned for contact is the same in every portfolio. Program adoption follows the rollout year in the officer table exactly (`{python} pct(adoption_matches_rollout)` agreement), so two portfolios adopted in FY2023, two in FY2024, and two in FY2025, while the last two had not adopted by the end of the program. Over the four years `{python} n(selected_people)` different people were selected, and `{python} n(selected_once)` of them only once.

The timing lines up with the cohorts used in this notebook. `{python} pct(gave_in_assignment_year)` of selected donors gave in their assignment year and `{python} pct(major_in_assignment_year)` were major donors that year, so a donor assigned in FY t is an eligible, non-major donor at the end of FY t, and the outcome of interest is whether they become major in FY t+1. The rest of this section matches each assignment year to the cohort with the same t.

### Who Gets Selected

```{python}
#| label: cultivation-selection
# match cultivation assignments to cohorts and compare selected, held-out, and non-selected donors

cult_cohorts = (
    feat.filter(pl.col("t").is_between(2022, 2025))
    .join(cult.select("constituent_id", "t", "contacted", "program_adopted"), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
    .with_columns(
        group=pl.when(pl.col("contacted").is_null()).then(pl.lit("not selected"))
        .when(pl.col("contacted")).then(pl.lit("selected, contacted"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("selected, held out")),
        prior_rank=pl.col("prior_total").rank(descending=True).over("t") / pl.len().over("t"),
    )
)
selected_share_of_eligible = cult_cohorts["contacted"].is_not_null().mean()
selected_in_eligible = cult.join(cult_cohorts.select("constituent_id", "t"), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="semi").height / cult.height
median_rank_selected = cult_cohorts.filter(pl.col("contacted").is_not_null())["prior_rank"].median()

selection_profile = (
    cult_cohorts.group_by("group")
    .agg(
        donor_years=pl.len(),
        median_prior_total=pl.col("prior_total").median(),
        former_major=pl.col("former_major").mean(),
        gave_5_of_5_years=(pl.col("years_last5") == 5).mean(),
        soft_credit_before=pl.col("soft_before").mean(),
        upgrade_gift=pl.col("upgrade_gift").mean(),
        converted_next_year=pl.col("converted").mean(),
    )
    .sort("group")
)
show(selection_profile, pct_cols=["former_major", "gave_5_of_5_years", "soft_credit_before", "upgrade_gift", "converted_next_year"], pct_digits=2, caption="Selected, held-out, and non-selected donors compared")
```

Selection draws almost entirely from the eligible population (`{python} pct(selected_in_eligible)` of selected donors are eligible in their cohort) and covers about `{python} pct(selected_share_of_eligible)` of it each year. Officers pick from the top of the giving distribution: the median selected donor ranks in the top `{python} pct(median_rank_selected)` of eligible donors by prior-year giving. Compared with donors who were not selected, they are much more likely to be former major donors, to have given in all of the last five years, to have a past soft credit, and to have made an upgrade gift, which are the same signals found in the giving behavior section. The contacted and held-out groups look alike on all of these measures, which is what random assignment should produce.

### Effect of Contact

The held-out donors were selected in the same way as the contacted donors but were not contacted, so comparing the two groups estimates what contact itself does.

```{python}
#| label: contact-effect
# difference in 12 month conversion between contacted and held-out donors, with a normal-approximation 95% interval

import math

def effect_row(label, df):
    treated = df.filter(pl.col("contacted") == True)
    control = df.filter(pl.col("contacted") == False)
    p1, n1 = treated["converted"].mean(), treated.height
    p0, n0 = control["converted"].mean(), control.height
    se = math.sqrt(p1 * (1 - p1) / n1 + p0 * (1 - p0) / n0)
    diff = p1 - p0
    return {"group": label, "contacted": n1, "contacted_rate": p1, "held_out": n0, "held_out_rate": p0,
            "difference": diff, "ci_low": diff - 1.96 * se, "ci_high": diff + 1.96 * se}

selected_only = cult_cohorts.filter(pl.col("contacted").is_not_null())
effects = pl.DataFrame([
    effect_row("all selected donors", selected_only),
    effect_row("portfolios that had adopted the program", selected_only.filter(pl.col("program_adopted"))),
    effect_row("portfolios that had not adopted", selected_only.filter(~pl.col("program_adopted"))),
    effect_row("never-major donors only", selected_only.filter(~pl.col("former_major"))),
])
eff = {r["group"]: r for r in effects.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(effects, pct_cols=["contacted_rate", "held_out_rate", "difference", "ci_low", "ci_high"], pct_digits=2, caption="Contacted minus held-out conversion, with 95% intervals")
```

Contact roughly doubles the chance of becoming a major donor the next year: `{python} pct(eff["all selected donors"]["contacted_rate"], 2)` for contacted donors versus `{python} pct(eff["all selected donors"]["held_out_rate"], 2)` for held-out donors, a difference of `{python} pp(eff["all selected donors"]["difference"])` percentage points (95% interval `{python} pp(eff["all selected donors"]["ci_low"])` to `{python} pp(eff["all selected donors"]["ci_high"])`). The effect holds for never-major donors, who convert at `{python} pct(eff["never-major donors only"]["contacted_rate"], 2)` when contacted and `{python} pct(eff["never-major donors only"]["held_out_rate"], 2)` when held out. It is concentrated in portfolios that had adopted the program, where the difference is `{python} pp(eff["portfolios that had adopted the program"]["difference"])` points. In portfolios that had not adopted it, the difference is `{python} pp(eff["portfolios that had not adopted"]["difference"])` points and the interval includes zero. These groups are small, so the program comparison is suggestive rather than settled, but contact itself clearly matters.

### How Much Conversion Runs Through the Program

```{python}
#| label: cultivation-share

def program_share(t):
    new_next = (
        panel.filter((pl.col("fy") == t + 1) & pl.col("major"))
        .join(panel.filter((pl.col("fy") == t) & pl.col("major")), on="constituent_id", how="anti")
    )
    sel = cult.filter(pl.col("t") == t)
    return {
        "cohort": t,
        "new_majors_next_year": new_next.height,
        "selected_in_fy_t": new_next.join(sel, on="constituent_id", how="semi").height,
        "contacted_in_fy_t": new_next.join(sel.filter(pl.col("contacted")), on="constituent_id", how="semi").height,
    }

program_shares = pl.DataFrame([program_share(t) for t in range(2022, 2026)])
ps_tot = program_shares.select(pl.exclude("cohort").sum()).row(0, named=True)

# within prior-giving bands: contacted, held out, and not selected
band_groups = (
```
